titlePattern.gap: Every top result is a product or category page; none says whether an extension column is worth it or how much it costs in stability. Ours leads with the keyword and the tall-photographer verdict.

commonPoints: An extension column adds height to an existing tripod (Benro, B&H, Javelin).
It collapses short for travel (Benro 7.9 in, Sunwayfoto 7.4 in).
Carbon fiber keeps it light (Benro, Sunwayfoto).
It must match the tripod's thread or series (Benro series sizes, Sunwayfoto 1/4"/3/8").

ourGain.point: An add-on column has the same lever and inertia penalty as a raised built-in column: fitting a column cost about 15% stiffness and vibrations decayed four times slower at full extension (The Center Column), while carbon columns lost 65% of yaw stiffness vs 29% for aluminum.

Rule by inches short: viewfinder within about 3 in of eye level = built-in column; 3 to 8 in short = extension column with light kit in calm air; more than 8 in short = taller legs. Worked example: 6'2" photographer (eye about 69-70 in) on 55 in legs plus 6 in head and camera is about 6 to 10 in short.

Owners use a screw-on column for occasional standing use, not every shot: briscoetab (Rokslide) gets 3-8 in from a screw-on Leofoto column and says an inch or two has little effect but full extension does, especially in wind; pyrotechnic added a column because his RRS legs were not high enough to use standing.
